newsitem.title: INDIA: IMF's Camdessus praises India's economic reforms.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Camdessus praises India's economic reforms.

text.p: International Monetary Fund managing director Michel Camdessus lauded India's economic liberalisation programme and said its policies were on the right track, local news agencies said on Monday.

"You are on the right track, doing the right thing," the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Camdessus as saying late on Sunday at a banquet hosted by Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor C. Rangarajan in the southern city of Madras.
"I congratulate the key architects who led this transformation, those who supported it and those who are carrying the reforms further," he said.
India began liberalising its economy in 1991 under former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, dismantling decades-old socialist controls.
Camdessus, who arrived in India on Saturday on a four-day visit, also praised the RBI for prudent management of the nation's monetary system.
The Business Standard newspaper quoted Camdessus as congratulating Finance Minister P. Chidambaram for "taking bold steps" in the 1997/98 (April-March) federal budget presented on Friday.
Chidambaram cut taxes and slashed import duties in the budget. In two special trading sessions after the announcements, Indian stocks jumped around 10 percent.
Camdessus was to meet chief minister Pratap Singh Rane of the western state of Goa on Monday and Tuesday. Prabhakar Narvekar, who is retiring as deputy IMF managing director, is from Goa.
The IMF chief also was scheduled to meet Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda and Chidambaram in New Delhi on Wednesday.
From India, Camdessus was set to travel to Hong Kong to address a major financial forum on March 7.
